title: Offline RFID Attendance
summary: An embedded attendance application designed for workplaces that need local operation without a continuous network connection.
problem: Attendance events must remain usable when internet access or a local server is unavailable.
approach: Integrated RFID and serial workflows with a Raspberry Pi application.
Built a Tkinter interface for attendance interactions.
Designed around local timekeeping, employee updates and spreadsheet export through USB storage.
outcome: An offline attendance workflow bringing card input, local records and removable-storage exchange together.
role: Python application development and hardware integration

sections.title: Attendance without a network dependency
body: The terminal records employee check-in and check-out locally, without requiring an internet connection or local server. It was developed as a custom attendance application for a food-industry setting in Tabriz.

sections.title: A local source of time
body: A DS1307 real-time-clock module synchronizes the Raspberry Pi clock when the device starts, providing the time source for attendance records.

sections.title: USB import and export
body: An employee list is loaded through USB. The application records attendance events in spreadsheet files, detects inserted removable storage and transfers the event files for collection.

sections.title: Embedded interaction
body: Python and Tkinter implement the local interface. Serial communication connects the RFID workflow, while the Raspberry Pi, RF01D reader and custom PCB form the device platform.

contribution: My work covered the Python/Tkinter attendance application and hardware integration for RFID interactions, local timekeeping and USB-based data exchange.
result: An offline attendance workflow bringing card input, local records and removable-storage exchange together.
decisionNotes: The Raspberry Pi application records attendance locally, uses a DS1307 RTC to set the device clock at startup, and imports employee data or exports event files through USB storage. Serial communication connects the RF01D reader to the local workflow.
validationNotes: A standalone attendance-system test recording shows the terminal workflow, and the public repository documents local attendance records, RTC timekeeping and USB exchange. These are implementation and demonstration artifacts; no timing-accuracy, record-integrity or long-duration reliability measurement is supplied.
